name: TX-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Ellzey's massive financial advantage ($4.7M raised vs $44K)
Incumbent running with no expert-rated vulnerability
Markets price Democratic chances at just 6%
model.rationale: Ellzey holds a deep financial and incumbency advantage in a district that leans Republican by double digits, and prediction markets give Minton almost no chance. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting vulnerability, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican win.
model.watch: A sudden influx of outside Democratic spending or a polling surprise could signal a closer race than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jake Ellzey, the Republican incumbent, is seeking reelection in a North Texas district that voted Republican by about 11 points at the presidential level. He has raised roughly $4.7 million and holds $2.5 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Danny Minton has raised about $44,000. No independent polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest.

Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 6% chance of an upset. The combination of the district's partisan lean, Ellzey's incumbency and financial dominance, and the absence of any visible Democratic outside spending makes Minton's path very narrow, though the lack of polling leaves some uncertainty around the exact margin.
